rationale: An informative recombinant placing the candidate outside the causal block is positional exclusion, the strongest available.
A high-confidence coordinate or liftover placing the gene outside the interval excludes it positionally.
Clear non-cosegregation in F2/F2:3 with adequate genotyping quality is genetic exclusion.
Phenotyping or genotyping QC flags, penetrance, or a linked QTL make a discordance uninterpretable.
Full CDS and splice boundaries read at the required coverage with no parental difference rejects the coding hypothesis only.
Partial coverage cannot reject a coding hypothesis; the unexamined scope is recorded instead.
A confirmed variant contradicting the expected inheritance or direction weakens the coding hypothesis.
A high-quality structural comparison finding no expected SV rejects the SV hypothesis only.
Expression clearly inconsistent with the relevant tissue and stage weakens the expression hypothesis; it is not a gene-level exclusion.
A source-backed mutant phenotype in the opposite direction weakens the candidate without excluding it.
One-to-one orthology unsupported while an alternate paralog is strongly supported is a tie-break, not an exclusion.
A subfamily or domain-architecture mismatch weakens the candidate relative to its siblings.
An assay that did not run is not evidence about the candidate.
Non-amplification can be a primer or template problem; it is not absence of the target.
Partially sequenced scope leaves the coding hypothesis unresolved.
An unmeasured tissue or stage is not non-expression.
Missing annotation is a reference limitation, not evidence against the candidate.
Absence of an ortholog hit does not exclude a lineage-specific or orphan candidate.
A low-quality assembly region cannot support any elimination.
A failed provider or API call carries no biological information.
